classification.difficultyReason: The slant side must first be found by Pythagoras from half the base and the altitude. Then three face types are summed. Same demand as the isosceles and right-triangle parts of p17-q5, without the surd work.

content.prompt: Find the surface area of the triangular prism.

answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the length of a sloping side of the triangular end. The altitude bisects the base, giving $16\div2=8\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}s^2&=8^2+15^2\\s&=17\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Front and back triangles:
$$A_{\text{triangles}}=\left(\frac{16\times15}{2}\right)\times2=240\text{ cm}^2$$
Side rectangles:
$$A_{\text{sides}}=9\times17+9\times17=306\text{ cm}^2$$
Bottom rectangle:
$$A_{\text{bottom}}=9\times16=144\text{ cm}^2$$
Total surface area:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{total}}&=240+306+144\\A_{\text{total}}&=690\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
